config.title: Build typed optimistic update shape

intro.title: Build typed optimistic update shape
intro.body: In this lesson, you will build a typed 'optimistic update shape' in TypeScript, which is a structured object that defines how to update your app's state immediately while a network request is in progress. You'll learn to use TypeScript's type system to ensure this shape is safe and predictable, preventing common errors. The core concept involves defining interfaces and types to model the data before and after an update. You'll work with basic TypeScript constructs like interfaces, type aliases, and optional properties. By the end, you'll have a reusable, type-safe blueprint for handling optimistic UI updates in your applications.
intro.usecase: Typed optimistic update shapes are essential in modern web applications where users expect immediate feedback. When you 'like' a post on social media, the heart icon instantly turns red while the actual API request processes in the background. In e-commerce carts, items appear added immediately while stock validation happens behind the scenes. This pattern prevents UI lag in dashboards updating metrics, collaborative tools syncing edits, or forms submitting data—all while maintaining type safety to catch errors during development rather than at runtime.

objectives: Construct a TypeScript interface to define the shape of an optimistic update
Implement a function that generates an optimistic update object from user input
Apply type annotations to ensure optimistic update properties match expected data structures
Configure a component to display optimistic updates with proper typing
Manipulate state to handle optimistic updates before server confirmation
Integrate typed optimistic updates into a simulated API call workflow
Initialize and render a UI that reflects optimistic updates with type safety

steps.title: Import TypeScript utilities for type definitions
steps.instruction: Import the TypeScript utilities that will be used to define types for optimistic updates. Add the import statement at the top of your file.
steps.hint: You'll need to import TypeScript's built-in utilities for working with types. Think about what utilities help define partial or optional structures.
steps.seedCode:
// Import TypeScript utilities for optimistic update types

// Your component or function will go here
steps.expectedOutcome: The file starts with an import statement bringing in TypeScript utilities needed for type definitions.
successCriteria: TypeScript utilities like Partial, Omit, or Pick are imported for use in type definitions.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track, but make sure to import specific TypeScript utilities like Partial or Omit.
steps.feedbackWrong: Check the import statement. You need to import TypeScript utilities for type manipulation.

steps.title: Define the base data interface
steps.instruction: Create a TypeScript interface named 'TodoItem' that defines the shape of a todo item with 'id' (number), 'title' (string), and 'completed' (boolean) properties.
steps.hint: Use the 'interface' keyword followed by the interface name and property definitions with type annotations.
steps.expectedOutcome: A TodoItem interface is created with the correct property types.
successCriteria: The TodoItem interface exists with id: number, title: string, and completed: boolean properties.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're close. Make sure all three properties (id, title, completed) are included with the correct types.
steps.feedbackWrong: The interface definition is missing or incorrect. Remember to use the 'interface' keyword and define all three properties with their types.

steps.title: Create the optimistic update state interface
steps.instruction: Define a TypeScript interface named OptimisticUpdateState that represents the state of an optimistic update. Include a boolean property 'isPending' and a generic property 'data' of type T (where T will be the data type being updated).
steps.hint: Use the 'interface' keyword to define the structure. The generic type T allows this interface to work with different data types.
steps.expectedOutcome: An interface definition that can represent optimistic update states with pending status and temporary data.
successCriteria: The OptimisticUpdateState interface is defined with 'isPending: boolean' and 'data: T' properties, using generic type T.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track, but make sure to include both required properties: 'isPending' (boolean) and 'data' (generic type T).
steps.feedbackWrong: The interface definition doesn't match the requirements. Remember to create an interface named OptimisticUpdateState with 'isPending: boolean' and 'data: T' properties.

steps.title: Define the optimistic update shape type
steps.instruction: Create a new TypeScript type named 'OptimisticUpdateShape' that combines the TodoItem interface with the OptimisticUpdateState interface using an intersection type.
steps.hint: Use the 'type' keyword followed by the type name and an equals sign. Then combine the two existing interfaces using the '&' operator.
steps.analogousExample:
// Example: combining two types with intersection
type CombinedShape = BaseData & UpdateState;
steps.expectedOutcome: You will have a new type that represents the complete shape of an optimistic update, including both the data and the optimistic state properties.
successCriteria: The OptimisticUpdateShape type is defined using an intersection type that combines TodoItem and OptimisticUpdateState.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track, but make sure you're using an intersection type with the '&' operator to combine both interfaces.
steps.feedbackWrong: The OptimisticUpdateShape type isn't defined correctly. Remember to use the 'type' keyword and combine both interfaces with an intersection.

steps.title: Create a helper type for optimistic update actions
steps.instruction: Define a new type named 'OptimisticUpdateAction' that can be either 'add', 'update', or 'delete' using a TypeScript union type.
steps.hint: Use the 'type' keyword with a union of string literal types separated by the '|' operator.
steps.analogousExample:
// Example: a union type for status
type Status = 'pending' | 'success' | 'error';
steps.expectedOutcome: You will have a union type that defines the possible optimistic update actions.
successCriteria: The code includes a type named 'OptimisticUpdateAction' defined as a union of the string literals 'add', 'update', and 'delete'.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track, but ensure the type is named exactly 'OptimisticUpdateAction' and includes all three string literals: 'add', 'update', 'delete'.
steps.feedbackWrong: The OptimisticUpdateAction type is missing or incorrect. Define a union type with the three specified string literal values.

steps.title: Define the optimistic update result type
steps.instruction: Create a TypeScript type named 'OptimisticUpdateResult' that represents the possible outcomes of an optimistic update operation. This type should be a union type that can be either 'success' with a data payload or 'error' with an error message.
steps.hint: Use a union type with discriminated unions. You can define each possible outcome as an object type with a 'status' property and additional data properties.
steps.analogousExample:
// Example: A result type for a network operation
type NetworkResult = { status: 'success'; data: string } | { status: 'error'; message: string };
steps.expectedOutcome: You should have a new type definition for 'OptimisticUpdateResult' that properly models the possible outcomes of optimistic updates.
successCriteria: The 'OptimisticUpdateResult' type is defined as a union type with at least 'success' and 'error' variants, each with appropriate properties.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track, but make sure OptimisticUpdateResult is a proper union type with both success and error variants. Check that each variant has the necessary properties.
steps.feedbackWrong: The OptimisticUpdateResult type isn't defined correctly. It should be a union type that can represent both successful outcomes (with data) and error outcomes (with error message).

steps.title: Create a sample data object
steps.instruction: Create a sample data object named 'sampleTodo' that conforms to the TodoItem interface.
steps.hint: Declare a constant variable with the name 'sampleTodo' and assign it an object with the required properties from TodoItem: id, title, and completed.
steps.expectedOutcome: A typed constant 'sampleTodo' is created with valid TodoItem properties.
successCriteria: The code includes a constant named 'sampleTodo' that has the required id (string), title (string), and completed (boolean) properties.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're close. Make sure your 'sampleTodo' object has all three required properties: id (string), title (string), and completed (boolean).
steps.feedbackWrong: The sample data object is missing or incorrect. Create a constant named 'sampleTodo' with an object containing id, title, and completed properties that match the TodoItem interface.

steps.title: Create an optimistic update state object
steps.instruction: Create a state object named 'optimisticState' that uses the OptimisticUpdateShape type with the sample todo data.
steps.hint: Declare a constant variable with the type annotation and assign it an object matching the shape.
steps.expectedOutcome: A typed state object 'optimisticState' is created with proper type annotation.
successCriteria: The 'optimisticState' object is declared with type OptimisticUpdateShape and contains valid todo data.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're close. Make sure the object has the correct type annotation and contains the required properties.
steps.feedbackWrong: The optimisticState object is missing or doesn't match the required type shape.

steps.title: Define a function to apply optimistic update
steps.instruction: Create a TypeScript function named applyOptimisticUpdate that takes a TodoItem and an OptimisticUpdateAction as parameters and returns an OptimisticUpdateResult.
steps.hint: Define the function with explicit parameter types and return type annotation. Inside, create a result object matching the OptimisticUpdateResult interface.
steps.expectedOutcome: A typed function that accepts a TodoItem and an OptimisticUpdateAction, and returns an OptimisticUpdateResult object.
successCriteria: The applyOptimisticUpdate function is defined with correct parameter types and return type, and returns an object matching OptimisticUpdateResult.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're close. Make sure the function has the correct name, parameter types, and returns an OptimisticUpdateResult object.
steps.feedbackWrong: The function is missing or has incorrect types. Review the required parameters and return type.

steps.title: Test the typed optimistic update shape
steps.instruction: Write a test case that demonstrates how the typed optimistic update shape works by creating a function named testOptimisticUpdate that calls applyOptimisticUpdate with sample data and logs the result.
steps.hint: Create a function that uses your existing applyOptimisticUpdate function with the sample data object and optimisticState object, then console.log the result to verify the type safety.
steps.expectedOutcome: A test function that demonstrates the typed optimistic update shape by calling applyOptimisticUpdate and logging the result to verify type safety.
successCriteria: The testOptimisticUpdate function is defined, calls applyOptimisticUpdate with appropriate arguments, and logs the result to the console.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track, but make sure your test function calls applyOptimisticUpdate with the appropriate arguments and logs the result to verify type safety.
steps.feedbackWrong: The test function doesn't properly demonstrate the typed optimistic update shape. Review how to call applyOptimisticUpdate and log the result to verify type safety.
